ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a Full-bridge VSI powered by the DC input Vin. The inverter output terminal is labeled VR, and then a series inductor L is connected; the node after the inductor is connected to a parallel branch, in which the capacitor C is connected to the lower return line, and the resistor R is also connected between the same output node and the return line. Reasoning calculation: The given output fundamental frequency f = 50 Hz, modulation index ma = 0.7, and DC input Vdc = 100 V. According to the specified method, the fundamental peak value of the bridge-arm output of a single-phase full-bridge unipolar PWM is V1,bridge = ma Vdc = 0.7 × 100 = 70 V. The filter is a series L followed by a parallel C-R, and the magnitude transfer function of Vo with respect to the bridge output fundamental is |H| = 1 / sqrt((1 - ω^2LC)^2 + (ωL/R)^2), where ω = 2πf = 2π × 50 rad/s. Substituting L = 9.55 mH = 9.55×10^-3 H, C = 63.66 μF = 63.66×10^-6 F, R = 5 Ω: ω^2LC ≈ 0.0600, ωL/R ≈ 0.600. Therefore |H| ≈ 1 / sqrt((1 - 0.0600)^2 + 0.600^2) ≈ 0.896. Thus the output voltage fundamental amplitude Vo1 = 70 × |H| ≈ 62.75 V.
